passage.title: Leaders Who Serve
paras: Look around this room. Every one of you will lead something one day: a team, a family, a business, perhaps a country. So let me ask you a question. When you lead, will you rule, or will you serve? History is full of rulers who were feared and forgotten. It is also full of servants who were loved and remembered. I stand here to argue that the greatest leaders are not the loudest, the richest or the strongest. They are the ones who serve.
First, servant leaders earn trust. When people see a leader who carries the heaviest box, eats last and listens first, they follow willingly. Fear makes people obey; trust makes them give their best.

Second, servant leaders build other leaders. A leader who serves teaches, delegates and lets others grow. When that leader leaves, the team carries on. A ruler who keeps all the power leaves nothing behind but a gap.

Third, servant leadership is not weakness. It takes courage to admit a mistake, patience to hear criticism and strength to put others first. The honour of leadership is the responsibility that comes with it.
Some will say that people need a strong hand. But strength and service are not opposites. The strongest leaders are those who use their strength for others.
So when your turn comes, and it will, do not ask, 'How can I be obeyed?' Ask, 'How can I help?' Serve, and you will lead.
